questions.prompt: A boutique HIIT owner sells dozens of intro offers a month, but her member count barely moves. What do you ask first?

options.text: How many intro buyers go on to become members?
How many stations are set up in each room?
Which payment processor do you use now?
How many coaches are on the schedule?

questions.reveal: Guest-to-member conversion is where the money is. Her answer tells you whether to lead with follow-up sequences.

questions.prompt: In this training, what gives a profitable studio or gym its steady base of income?

options.text: Drop-ins paid at the door for each class
Retail sales of water and grip socks
Recurring memberships billed automatically
Workshops run a few times each year

questions.reveal: Memberships on autopay are the predictable base. Packs, drop-ins and intro offers are the on-ramp to them.

questions.prompt: A gym's 6 a.m. bootcamp rarely has more than three people. What's the business question underneath?

options.text: Is the coach certified to teach bootcamp?
Does the class earn more than the coach costs?
Does the class need its own waiver form?
Does the room map have enough spots?

questions.reveal: Each class has to cover the coach's time. Thin classes can earn less than the coach is worth.

questions.prompt: Per the Health & Fitness Association, which age group of US fitness members grew fastest in 2025?

options.text: Members aged 18 to 24
Members aged 25 to 34
Members aged 35 to 44
Members aged 65 and over

questions.reveal: Members 65 and over grew fastest. ACSM's 2026 survey also ranks programs for older adults second.

questions.prompt: An owner says payroll takes her hours because she counts each coach's classes by hand. What do you show?

options.text: The free app's push notifications
Pay rates and payroll reports in Momence
The Spot Filler add-on settings
The community page for members

questions.reveal: Pay rates per coach plus payroll reports show what each person is owed, without counting by hand.

questions.prompt: What's accurate about staff pay in Momence?

options.text: It shows what's owed; pay happens outside
It pays coaches by direct deposit weekly
It allows only one hourly rate per coach
It needs a separate payroll add-on to run

questions.reveal: Momence tracks rates and reports what's owed. The owner still pays staff outside Momence.

questions.prompt: A rider is about to hit her 100th class. How does a studio on Momence make sure nobody misses it?

options.text: The coach keeps a list of riders in a notebook
Staff search the reports by hand each Friday
The rider tells the front desk about it herself
Visit count on the roster and a milestone email

questions.reveal: Visit counts show at check-in, and a milestone sequence can email the client automatically.

questions.prompt: A gym owner wants coaches to see only their own classes, while the front desk handles messages and sales. What do you show?

options.text: One shared login for all of the staff
A separate account for each coach
Staff roles with their own permissions
The free app with a staff setting on

questions.reveal: Roles control what each person sees and does, so coaches check people in and the desk gets the inbox and point of sale.

questions.prompt: A strength coach writes an individual program for every client and tracks their lifts. What do you show?

options.text: Custom checkout questions about goals
Video on demand with recorded classes
Workouts with scored exercises and programs
The community page with weekly posts

questions.reveal: Workouts hold exercises scored in pounds, reps or rounds, built into programs for a group or one person.

questions.prompt: A coaching client's pack runs out mid-month. What can Momence do with the pack?

options.text: Hold her bookings until she pays in person
Turn the pack into a membership on its own
Send a refill link only on the 1st
Refill it when the last credit is used

questions.reveal: Packs can auto-refill when credits run out, on an interval, or whichever comes first.

questions.prompt: A sports training facility runs a six-week youth skills program. Families should pay once and be enrolled in every session. What fits?

options.text: A term that enrolls them in all sessions
Six drop-ins booked a week at a time
A membership with a six-class limit
An appointment the coach books weekly

questions.reveal: A term enrolls the client in every session of a multi-week series at once, paid up front or on a plan.

questions.prompt: A bootcamp owner runs her community in a Facebook group and wants it inside her studio's app. What do you show?

options.text: A group text to every member weekly
The community page in the free app
The inbox with a shared staff thread
A monthly newsletter from the CRM

questions.reveal: The community page lets members see posts and like and comment on them in the app, sent to everyone or a segment.

questions.prompt: A prospect says new clients give up at her system's login screen. What's your strongest demo move?

options.text: Show the report of new clients by month
Explain how passwords keep cards safe
Open the inbox and show a client thread
Book on her site, then on a Momence site

questions.reveal: Let her see the difference. Her own login wall next to Momence's one-page checkout makes the point.

questions.prompt: A small-group trainer moving off paper sign-up sheets is comparing systems. What does this training say she needs most?

options.text: A branded app before anything else
Simplicity over a long list of features
Every add-on so she never upgrades
A custom build done by onboarding

questions.reveal: First-time software buyers need it simple. Show the few screens that replace her paper, not the whole platform.

questions.prompt: Asked whether video ads can be built in the ads manager, you aren't sure. What do you say?

options.text: “Yes, you'll build everything right here.”
“No, Meta ads don't work with Momence.”
“Let me confirm that and get back to you.”
“Most studios don't run video ads now.”

questions.reveal: A confident guess you have to walk back costs more trust than a short “let me confirm.”

questions.prompt: An owner says her team reaches out to every month-to-month member by hand before renewal. What do you show?

options.text: Auto-renewing memberships and sequences
A spreadsheet export of every member
A staff task list for weekly calls
Roster flags for birthdays and visits

questions.reveal: Memberships renew and bill automatically, and sequences can trigger on events like a membership expiring.

questions.prompt: A founder says, “I need to talk to my husband about the cost.” What's the best next step?

options.text: Book a dated call and invite him to it
Send pricing and wait for her email
Offer a discount if she signs today
Ask her to decide before he weighs in

questions.reveal: Get a decision date and bring the other decision-maker into the next call, with a recap he can read first.

questions.prompt: Which discovery question best tells you whether to show appointments next to classes?

options.text: How many members do you have today?
What time is your busiest class?
How did you choose your studio name?
Do you sell PT, scans or consults too?

questions.reveal: If she sells personal training, scans or consults, show them as appointments in the same system as her classes.

questions.prompt: How does this training say to handle a real strength in the prospect's current tool?

options.text: Point out its bugs before she brings them up
Acknowledge it, then show where we're better
Skip past it and move on to our marketing
Say all tools have the same features now

questions.reveal: Acknowledge what their tool does well, then show where Momence is better for them. Never knock the competitor.

questions.prompt: A cycling studio opens in December, and the founder plans to wait until then to set up software. What do you point out?

options.text: Onboarding can't start before the doors open
She can't take any payments until she opens
Presales and founding memberships start sooner
Spot Filler works best from her first week

questions.reveal: Presales and founding memberships can sell before opening, and a membership can activate on the client's first class.
